summary: Both turn-1 MUST-FIXes are discharged, and the blocker repair is the strongest work in either draft this turn. All seven join blockers are now named with typed dispositions rather than a blanket inapplicability, and the two dispositions I could check at bytes both hold: BLK-7's REPAIRED-IN-V4 claim is exact — doctor v4 quotes the false v1 clause and records finding B2 and CONTRA-8 as REPAIRED, so v4 does not assert it — and the new provenance paragraph correctly identifies the join as reviewing doctor v1 and permission v1, which I confirmed from the verdict's own recordedInputs.subjects. BLK-3 and BLK-4 are handled better than I asked: rather than declaring them inapplicable, the entry retains them for the component tails it keeps inside DR-105 and routes BLK-4's state-class half to DR-124. The v4/D-035 rebase is complete and the six-row digest table is correct. One turn-1 SHOULD-FIX is only half discharged: permissionRef is genuinely closed, but the PT-NET-EGRESS branch is the same conditional reworded, now under a heading asserting closure, and I verified doctor v4 does not settle it.

turn1Findings.C2-D032-01: LANDED-VERIFIED, and exceeded. Clause 5 now names all seven blockers by id with typed dispositions. The three I found unaddressed are addressed: BLK-2 (CA-3 tokenless probes) is STILL-ROUTED to the host-effect contract with host-executed probes placed outside DR-105 and held fail-closed until that contract names them; BLK-6 (the four DR-105 tokens describing doctor's unconsented default reads) is DISCHARGED-AS-INAPPLICABLE under Option B with doctor's no-silent-downgrade rule preserved; BLK-7 is REPAIRED-IN-V4. The fourth, BLK-4, which I found surviving in the component-tail case, is now handled precisely on that point: 'STILL-ROUTED to DR-124 for the grant journal's state class, and only arises on component tails that remain in DR-105. Host doctor writes no grant journal.' BLK-3 likewise gains a retention clause — 'RETAINED for component tails inside DR-105' — which is more honest than the blanket inapplicability the turn-1 draft implied. The typed vocabulary (STILL-ROUTED, DISCHARGED-AS-INAPPLICABLE, DISCHARGED, REPAIRED-IN-V4) distinguishes disposal from routing, which is what 'stated not waved' requires.
turn1Findings.C2-D032-02: LANDED-VERIFIED. 'Readiness effect. Zero. No file 08 status cell moves. No candidate is applied. No blueprint is authorized.' And 'Reversibility. Class: total before any conforming successor (host-effect contract, doctor v5, permission v2) lands. After those land, overturn also requires their owning-authority supersession. Overturn: C-D032.' The reversibility class carries the temporal boundary the adopted D-028/D-029/D-030 use, and it names the three dependent classes clause 7 creates, which is more specific than the siblings manage.
turn1Findings.C2-D032-03: PARTIALLY LANDED. The permissionRef half is fully discharged: clause 6 rules it 'permanently reserved (not withdrawn as a schema member; never populated for host acts)', which picks one of the two outcomes I flagged and states the consequence for each. The PT-NET-EGRESS half is not discharged; it is the same conditional in declarative grammar, now under a heading claiming both are closed. Raised as C2T2-D032-01.
turn1Findings.C2-D032-04: LANDED-VERIFIED, and exceeded. The measured-inputs table carries six rows and every digest I re-measured is correct: file 08 5e1a75a5…, COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md 9d41c5ba…, doctor-contract.v4.json df2e7175…, permission-truth-tables.v1.json 0f73f31c…, join review 538f3681…, and the row labelled 'D-035 verdict' d6328807…. The re-measurement clause is restored. Beyond the pins, a new standing paragraph does the rebase work I asked for and more: it identifies the join as doctor v1 plus permission v1, states it is not a review of v4, records permission v1 as CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and independently REJECTED at 3 blockers, and records doctor v4 as the accepted design contract per D-035 and still CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED. The stale v2 citations are gone. One label defect remains, raised as C2T2-D032-N1.

objections.claim: Clause 6 is headed 'Disjunctions closed' but only one of the two is closed. The PT-NET-EGRESS branch is the turn-1 conditional restated in declarative grammar, its governing fact is undecided, and doctor v4 does not settle it.
objections.evidence: Turn 1 read: 'PT-NET-EGRESS's slice-1 posture, if host-executed doctor egress, re-binds to DR-114's consent record; if component-executed, it stays DR-105.' Turn 2 reads: 'Slice-1 doctor egress that is host-executed re-binds to DR-114's consent record; component-executed egress stays DR-105 / PT-NET-EGRESS.' The grammar changed from conditional to relative-clause; the content is identical. Both give a rule keyed on which branch obtains, and neither states which does. My turn-1 finding was precisely that the rule was correct but the branch fact undecided, and offered two acceptable repairs: state which branch slice-1 doctor egress takes, or record explicitly that the branch is undecided and name where it is decided. Neither is taken, and the text is now placed under a heading asserting that the disjunctions are closed. I checked whether the branch is determinable from the artifact the entry now pins: doctor-contract.v4.json at df2e717555616db096e61548458f23b442f7f0e37b2d2461eabc2c33201e94b3 contains zero occurrences of 'host-executed' and zero of 'component-executed', against 8 occurrences of PT-NET-EGRESS and 37 of 'egress' — so v4 discusses egress extensively and never assigns its execution side. The branch is therefore genuinely open, which makes the second repair route the correct one and the closure claim inaccurate. This matters because clause 7 instructs that 'Successors must conform or contest': a successor author cannot conform to a rule whose antecedent is unsettled, and cannot tell from this entry whether the question is theirs to answer.
objections.proposedFix: Retitle clause 6 to reflect what it does — permissionRef closed, PT-NET-EGRESS routed — and add one sentence recording that the execution side of slice-1 doctor egress is not settled by doctor v4 and naming where it is decided, most plausibly DR-114 as part of the consented-probes/egress contract. If the coordinator believes v4 does settle it, cite the selector.

objections.claim: The measured-inputs row labelled 'D-035 verdict' pins a correct digest under a name that does not identify the file, and no artifact of that name exists.
objections.evidence: The table's fourth row reads 'D-035 verdict | d63288079bcc9d7a68e2de54069e83910eaaf3aa53c53707a45d5730908196b2'. No file matching D-035 exists in docs/coop/artifacts. I resolved the pin by hashing the tree: the digest is doctor-contract.v4.review-independent.json, the independent review of the v4 artifact, which D-035 recorded but did not itself produce. D-035 is a RULE-GOVERNED recording entry and has no adversarial verdict file, so a reader searching for a 'D-035 verdict' finds nothing and would have to hash the corpus as I did. The digest is correct and the artifact is real, so nothing is unresolvable — this is a naming defect, not a citation error. I record it because this corpus has already been bitten by exactly this class: DR-002's acceptance note documents the naming trap where check-evidence-v11.py's subject is evidence.v10, and DR-204 had to adjudicate a claim that two digests were unresolvable when they were execution pins misread as file pins.
objections.proposedFix: Relabel the row 'doctor-contract.v4.review-independent.json (the review D-035 records)'.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 10de7d1ccde16f17fb44318e30ab774e8a3139564077954206cbd4567a28ffd4 both times. No drift.

All seven join blockers are named: clause 5 carries BLK-1 through BLK-7 by id, each with a typed disposition. I re-read the verdict's $.blockers list to confirm the set is exactly seven and that the ids match.

BLK-7's disposition is exact, checked at bytes rather than accepted. The turn-2 entry claims 'REPAIRED-IN-V4 (v1 B2 / v2 repair)'. Measured: the string 'no DR-105 artifact' occurs once in doctor-contract.v1 and three times in v2 and v4. Inspecting the v4 occurrences, none is an assertion — one narrates the repair ('The v1 form of this bullet ended with the clause "and no DR-105 artifact exists in the measured tree". That clause was false at the reviewer's measurement moment…'), one is the repairLog entry for subject finding B2 with disposition REPAIRED, and one is the repairLog entry for CONTRA-8 with disposition REPAIRED and the note 'Same repair as subject blocker B2'. So v4 quotes and repairs rather than asserts, the repair landed at v2 as the entry says, and the B2/CONTRA-8 attribution is right.

The join's provenance claim is exact. The entry states '538f3681… is the join of doctor v1 and permission v1.' Measured from the verdict's own recordedInputs.subjects: permission-truth-tables.v1.json (DR-105) and doctor-contract.v1.json (DR-114). The verdict's header also carries documentClass CROSS-ARTIFACT-COHERENCE-REVIEW, binds NOTHING, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, and a scope line stating it is not a re-review of either subject — all consistent with the entry's characterization that it is not a review of v4.

The v4/D-035 rebase is complete. The stale doctor-contract.v2 citations from turn 1 are gone; v4 is pinned at df2e7175… and permission v1 at 0f73f31c…, both re-measured correct. The standing paragraph states permission v1 as CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and independently REJECTED at 3 blockers and doctor v4 as the D-035 accepted design contract, still CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED — consistent with file 08's DR-114 row at 5e1a75a5, which reads 'design contract ACCEPTED 2026-08-13 (D-035); the actor-join and fixture-execution halves remain open'.

Host-owner and fail-closed-until-host-contract, the axis the prompt names: present and materially stronger than turn 1. Clause 4 now names an accountable owner — 'Operability + security (DR-114's owners) jointly with Security + platform owners (DR-105's owners)' — and imposes a precondition: 'Before any CA-1 host head, CA-2, CA-3, or host CA-4 act is exercisable, a scoped host-effect authorization contract must exist, independently reviewed, and recorded by those owners. Until then those host acts stay fail-closed (CONSENT-REQUIRED / unexercisable).' Turn 1's clause 4 named an origin but no owner and no precondition. Alternatives adds a third option, 'Leave host authorization unowned. Rejected: fail-closed with no owner is the current defect', which names the gap this repairs.

No smuggled apply: clause 7 states 'This entry does not apply doctor v4 or permission v1. Successors must conform or contest. No row, join verdict, candidate standing, or blueprint authorization moves', and the readiness section repeats that no candidate is applied and no blueprint authorized. Clause 4 explicitly declines to mint the host-effect contract or any permission token. I checked the entry for any new token or effect-class name and found none.

D-000 clause 3 completeness, field by field: id, date, title, status, decision, alternatives (three, each with stated benefit and cost rather than dismissal), rationale via Honesty, decision type PREFERENCE-LADEN, reversibility class with temporal boundary, overturn procedure. Readiness effect present. Reviewer verdict and commit land at adoption.

The Alternatives section improved beyond what I raised: A and C now each carry a 'Strongest benefit' clause before the cost — A's 'one journal, one linearization, monotonic revoke across host and component' is a fair statement of what Option B gives up, which is the test of whether a rejected alternative got a real hearing.

The fourth-deliberate-non-token warrant, verified at turn 1 and unchanged, still holds: permission-truth-tables.v1's deliberateNonTokens is a four-member list whose fourth is host-initiated writes to a user-named output path, ruled NOT a component permission.

permission-truth-tables.v1's three independent-review blockers on their merits. I took the entry's characterization of its standing as CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and REJECTED at 3 blockers and did not re-adjudicate them.
D-036 as an entry, beyond noting that its Lane P step 3 and step 4 reference this one. D-036 is reviewed separately in this session against its own prompt.
